findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === never equal, full-day unavailable override ignored
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an unavailable-day override where start equals end. `===` on Dayjs objects compares object identity, never value equality, so it is always false. As a result a date override that should block the whole day sets dateOverrideExist but never matches the find, falls through to `if (dateOverrideExist) return true`, and the slot is reported as available when the host is unavailable, allowing bookings on blocked days.

findings.title: Date-override hit returns available without checking busy times
findings.body: After scanning dateOverrides, if any override covers the slot day the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` immediately. That early return skips the later `busy.every(...)` calendar/booking check. On any day with a date override, existing Cal bookings, calendar busy blocks, and selected-slot holds for that fixed host are ignored, so double-bookings become possible on override days.

findings.title: Working-hours end uses slot start, ignores event length
findings.body: The working-hours guard computes both `start` and `end` as `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` should be slot end (start + eventLength). An event that starts inside working hours but ends after them, e.g. 60-min event starting 30 min before close, passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test and is offered as bookable, causing bookings that overrun availability.

findings.title: Working-hours outside check inverted for split days and empty days
findings.body: The code uses `workingHours.find(h => slot outside h)` to decide the slot is outside working hours. If a user has two intervals in one day, e.g. morning and afternoon, a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon interval, so `find` succeeds and the valid slot is rejected. Conversely if no interval lists that weekday, `find` returns undefined and the code falls through to the busy check, treating a non-working day as available. Valid slots are hidden and invalid days can appear bookable.

findings.title: Date-override timezone used without fallback and via toString round-trip
findings.body: TimeRange.timeZone is optional, but getSlots does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` with no guard. When timeZone is missing, tz gets undefined and produces an invalid/NaN offset or throws, breaking slot generation for legacy overrides. Even when present, `override.start.toString()` serializes the instant in server-local format and re-parses it before converting, which is locale-dependent and fragile compared to using the Date directly with a fallback to organizerTimeZone.

findings.title: No test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
findings.body: The PR description claims it fixes date overrides of fixed hosts being ignored for round-robin events, which is implemented in the new checkIfIsAvailable filtering in viewer/slots.ts. The only test added covers the same UTC slots under a different invitee timezone for a single-user event. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event, fixed vs loose hosts, and conflicting date overrides, so the main claimed fix and the new working-hours/date-override branches are untested and regressions would not be caught.
